title: Why Can't You See Your Own Eyes Move?
pause_note: Short format v3 (2026-11-13): 20-30 s, claim first, loop ending

beats: You've never seen your own eyes move.
Look in a mirror. Look at your left eye, then your right.
You never see them move. But they do: a quick jump, several times a second.
During each jump, your brain hides the blur and stitches the gap.
Your phone's front camera shows you a split second late.
So on the screen, you catch them moving.
